title: Responsive Desktop Tablet Mobile Layout Devices
description: Make the ui-react design system, the framework OS shell (os-shell.tsx), and the OS playground automatically switch into mobile mode when viewport width drops below 768px, and add a desktop/tablet layout setting. Desktop is the current look. Tablet uses larger touch-friendly spacing/buttons via the existing .touch CSS scale, selectable in Settings. Mobile drops the tiling window manager for a tab-based canvas with a phone-optimized navbar and bottom-nav footer, and is automatic (not user-selectable) below the breakpoint. Implementation plan agreed with user covers: ui-react ElementsSurfaceChrome/layout storage helpers, os-shell device-driven chrome wiring + settings Layout select, Mode component mobile prop (single active window, no tab bar/drag/dock), mobile FooterNav + compact mobile navbar, .touch CSS additions for touch target sizing, and extending existing vitest suites.
summary:
Follow-up fix per dev feedback: "On mobile, windows have no focus button."

Root cause (confirmed via browser inspection on the "cad" app, which has 4+ windows on mobile): flattening every window into one tab stack means the tab bar can end up with several long tab labels ("semio · cad · shape", "semio · cad · building", ...) in a 375px viewport. The shared ModeDockTabBar reserves space for its trailing Focus/Close controls-cap two ways depending on tab count: (1) the plain path (≤1 tab) capped the tab area at a fixed `max-w-[calc(100%-var(--size-medium))]` — a hardcoded ~2-2.5rem "reserve" that's nowhere near the ~140px the two text+icon buttons actually need; (2) the chromeGrid path (2+ tabs, desktop's "per-tab active chrome" visual) sizes each tab column to `max-content` (unshrinkable) in a CSS grid with no horizontal scroll — with enough tabs the grid simply overflows past the controls column, pushing it off-screen entirely. Both are latent bugs in the shared component that essentially never manifested on desktop (panes are normally far wider than 375px) but are guaranteed to hit on a phone-width flattened stack.

Fix (ui/js/react/index.tsx): added an optional `mobile` prop to `ModeDockStack` (threaded from `Mode`'s new mobile-flattened-stack render call). When `mobile` is true, `ModeDockStack` never computes a `chromeGrid` (`!mobile && tabs.length > 1`), so it always takes the plain tab-bar path — the desktop-only "per-tab active chrome" grid visual is skipped on mobile, not removed for desktop. Fixed that plain path's tab-cap sizing at the root: replaced the fixed `max-w-[calc(100%-var(--size-medium))] shrink-0` with a real flex-shrink (`shrink`, relying on the sibling `min-w-0` + the tab list's existing `overflow-x-auto`), so the tab strip now correctly shrinks/scrolls to leave room for the `shrink-0` controls-cap regardless of tab count or label length — this also fixes the same latent issue for any narrow desktop pane, not just mobile. Also added `mode-dock-maximize`/`mode-dock-close` to the `.touch` CSS touch-target sizing rule (ui/styling/js/ui.css) alongside the existing `mode-dock-tab` entry, since these buttons are now load-bearing on touch devices.

Tests (ui/js/react/index.tsx in-source vitest): extended "Mode mobile" with an assertion that `mode-dock-maximize`/`mode-dock-close` render in the 2-window case, and a new case with 4 long-labeled windows asserting the chrome-grid slot (`mode-dock-chrome-column`) is never used on mobile and the controls-cap/tab-cap render via the plain structure instead. Full suites: 75/75 renderer tests pass; 207/216 ui-react tests pass (same 9 pre-existing/unrelated failures — CanvasPickMenu, PanelTabBar, SidePanel, tree helpers — as before this ticket; zero new failures from this change, including the existing desktop `chromeGrid`/multi-tab-maximize tests, confirming desktop is unaffected since `mobile` defaults to false everywhere except the new mobile call site).

Browser-verified on s-react-dev (port 6070) with `?plugin=cad` at 375x812: Focus and Close buttons are now visible and pinned at the right edge of the tab bar, with the (now correctly truncating/scrollable) window tabs on the left — confirmed via screenshot and DOM bounding-rect inspection (button fully within the 0-375 viewport). Note: this session had an unusually disruptive concurrent environment — another developer was mid-flight on a large, codebase-wide Command→Action rename (ticket RENAME-WINDOW-COMMAND-TO-ACTION) touching os-shell.tsx/ui-interpreter.tsx/index.tsx throughout, causing continuous forced HMR reloads that repeatedly interrupted live verification. The fix itself is orthogonal to that rename (pure CSS/prop-threading change) and both the static analysis and the screenshots obtained give high confidence it's correct.
